source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Hepatic encephalopathy, which is established by tremor and hallucinations after abrupt alcohol cessation without further evaluation.","B":"Wernicke encephalopathy, which is defined by marked autonomic hyperactivity and hallucinations after stopping alcohol.","C":"Alcohol withdrawal delirium, a severe withdrawal syndrome requiring prompt medical treatment and close monitoring.","D":"A primary psychotic disorder, which is more likely than withdrawal when severe tremor and autonomic hyperactivity follow alcohol cessation."}}
source_row.rationale: Alcohol withdrawal delirium is a severe withdrawal syndrome characterized by delirium with autonomic hyperactivity and can include hallucinations and marked tremor. It is medically dangerous and requires prompt treatment and monitoring rather than reassurance alone.
source_row.source_detail: Alcohol withdrawal delirium: severe withdrawal with delirium/autonomic activation; recommendations VI.7–VI.13 address close monitoring and active medical management. ASAM Clinical Practice Guideline 2020 remains the active ASAM alcohol-withdrawal guideline; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation: acute/complex alterations, emergency response and pathophysiologic adaptation. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.source_name: American Society of Addiction Medicine — Alcohol Withdrawal Management Guideline
source_row.stem: A hospitalized client with heavy alcohol use develops severe tremor, confusion, hallucinations, and marked autonomic hyperactivity after stopping alcohol. Which condition should the nurse suspect?
